patient.chief_complaint: Refractory focal seizures — episodes of fear, leftward head turning, and left-hand automatisms — persisting despite two antiepileptic drug trials; referred for inpatient epilepsy evaluation and consideration of surgical candidacy
patient.history_present_illness:
Ms. Patel is a 30-year-old right-handed South Asian woman admitted to the inpatient epilepsy monitoring unit for evaluation of drug-resistant focal seizures. Her seizure history began approximately two and a half years ago with stereotyped episodes characterized by a sudden rising fear, a chest-sinking sensation, and occasionally a brief smell that she describes as burning plastic. During most episodes her husband observes her to turn her head to the left, adopt a posture with the left arm flexed, and perform repetitive left-hand finger-plucking or rubbing automatisms. Awareness is impaired during the automatisms. Seizures typically last 40 to 90 seconds, after which she is confused and fatigued for 10 to 20 minutes. On approximately three occasions over the past year, a seizure has progressed to bilateral tonic-clonic activity. Seizure frequency has been two to four events per week despite therapy.

A standard brain MRI performed at seizure onset two years ago was reported as normal. A subsequent 1.5T epilepsy-protocol MRI performed six months later at her referring center was also read as showing no epileptogenic abnormality. These normal MRI results raised doubt about an epileptic etiology at her referring center; a psychiatry consultation concluded that the clinical picture was 'most consistent with psychogenic non-epileptic spells superimposed on a migrainous diathesis,' and a trial of psychotherapy and reduced antiepileptic medication was recommended. Her neurologist, however, observed that the semiology was highly stereotyped, occurred from sleep on two occasions, and was witnessed with a clear post-ictal phase, and declined to reduce medication.

She was initially started on levetiracetam titrated to 3000 mg per day, with no clinically meaningful reduction in seizure frequency after 18 months at therapeutic serum levels. Levetiracetam was subsequently tapered off and lamotrigine was introduced, titrated to 400 mg per day over eight months. Lamotrigine serum levels are therapeutic and the patient is fully adherent, but seizure frequency has not meaningfully decreased. She now meets criteria for drug-resistant focal epilepsy per the 2010 ILAE consensus definition. She is referred to this center for presurgical evaluation with long-term video-EEG, advanced imaging, and neuropsychological testing to localize the seizure focus and assess surgical candidacy.

results.title: Definition of drug-resistant epilepsy: consensus proposal by the ad hoc Task Force of the ILAE Commission on Therapeutic Strategies
results.summary: Drug-resistant epilepsy is defined as failure of adequate trials of two tolerated, appropriately chosen, and used antiepileptic drug schedules (whether as monotherapy or in combination) to achieve sustained seizure freedom. Early referral for presurgical evaluation is recommended once drug resistance criteria are met.

results.title: The contribution of 18F-FDG PET in preoperative epilepsy surgery evaluation for patients with temporal lobe epilepsy
results.summary: FDG-PET demonstrates ipsilateral temporal hypometabolism in approximately 70-85% of temporal lobe epilepsy cases, including MRI-negative TLE. PET is particularly valuable when MRI is non-localizing; concordance between PET hypometabolism and video-EEG lateralization supports surgical candidacy with reasonable seizure-free outcomes.

results.title: MRI-negative temporal lobe epilepsy: prevalence, outcomes, and the role of advanced presurgical evaluation
results.summary: Approximately 20-30% of temporal lobe epilepsy patients have normal MRI on standard sequences. Despite absence of structural lesion, interictal and ictal EEG lateralization combined with FDG-PET hypometabolism ipsilateral to the focus provide sufficient localization for surgical evaluation. Surgical outcomes in MRI-negative TLE are modestly lower than in HS-positive TLE (50-60% seizure freedom) but significantly superior to continued medical therapy.

results.title: Practice parameter: temporal lobe and localized neocortical resections for epilepsy
results.summary: Comprehensive presurgical evaluation including video-EEG, high-resolution MRI, and FDG-PET is recommended for drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Neuropsychological evaluation is essential to lateralize memory and assess surgical risk. In MRI-negative TLE with concordant multimodal data, surgical resection is a reasonable option with substantial chance of improved seizure control.

output.proposed: Lamotrigine 400 mg/day (current) with oral contraceptive pill (ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel); potential addition of a third antiepileptic agent
interactions: Oral contraceptives (ethinyl estradiol) induce UGT enzymes and significantly reduce lamotrigine plasma levels — typically by 40-60%. Breakthrough seizures during the active pill days and increased seizure frequency on stopping the pill are documented pharmacokinetic consequences.
Metformin: no clinically significant interaction with lamotrigine
Enzyme-inducing AEDs (carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital) would further reduce lamotrigine levels and reduce OCP efficacy — relevant if escalation is considered
contraindications: Sulfonamide allergy is documented; confirm sulfonamide class before prescribing zonisamide (sulfonamide-derived AED) as cross-reactivity risk exists
warnings: Lamotrigine levels must be monitored closely relative to OCP cycle phase; levels may be substantially lower during active pill-taking days and rise sharply during hormone-free week, leading to toxicity
If contraception method changes (e.g., OCP discontinuation), lamotrigine doses may require downward adjustment to avoid toxicity
Non-enzyme-inducing AEDs (lacosamide, levetiracetam, perampanel) are pharmacokinetically neutral with OCPs and with lamotrigine — preferred if adjunctive therapy is considered
Zonisamide is a sulfonamide derivative; use with caution or avoid given documented sulfonamide allergy
output.formulary_status: Lamotrigine on formulary. Lacosamide on formulary (requires prior authorization for add-on use). Perampanel on formulary.
alternatives: Lacosamide 100-200 mg twice daily (no interaction with OCP or lamotrigine; favorable tolerability profile; non-enzyme inducing)
Perampanel 2-12 mg once nightly (no significant pharmacokinetic interaction with lamotrigine at doses <12 mg; monitor for CNS side effects)
Clobazam 5-20 mg per day (non-enzyme-inducing benzodiazepine; adjunctive role; caution sedation)

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Drug-resistant focal epilepsy of right temporal lobe origin (MRI-negative)

differential.key_features: Normal MRI at two institutions anchored the referring psychiatry consultation toward PNES; however stereotyped semiology, ictal EEG correlate, post-ictal prolactin elevation, and occurrence from sleep exclude this diagnosis.

Frontal lobe seizures can have brief duration and head-turning; typically hypermotor, without prolonged post-ictal confusion; right anterior temporal EEG onset and PET hypometabolism argue against frontal origin.

differential.diagnosis: MRI-occult mesial temporal sclerosis or focal cortical dysplasia
differential.key_features: Hippocampal sclerosis may be missed on 1.5T MRI and occasionally on 3T; FCD type I/II can be radiologically occult; concordant multimodal data support right temporal focus regardless.
No myoclonic jerks, no generalized spike-wave on EEG, focal semiology with head-version and unilateral automatisms inconsistent with IGE.
No subacute cognitive or behavioral decline, no hyponatremia, no faciobrachial dystonic seizures; antibody panel would be needed if clinical course changes.

optimal_actions.action: Obtain detailed seizure history: semiology, aura character, automatism laterality, head-version direction, post-ictal features, nocturnal occurrence, and frequency on current therapy.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Stereotyped focal seizures with right-temporal aura (fear, rising sensation, olfactory), left-sided automatisms and head-version (contralateral to right-sided focus), post-ictal confusion — consistent with right temporal lobe origin.
Interictal examination nonfocal; absence of focal deficits consistent with non-dominant (right) temporal localization.

optimal_actions.action: Obtain CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel, AED levels, and prolactin (if drawn within 20 minutes post-event) to confirm therapeutic drug levels and exclude metabolic provocation.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Therapeutic lamotrigine level confirming true pharmacological failure (not sub-therapeutic dosing); elevated prolactin supporting recent convulsive event; normal metabolic panel excluding provoked seizure.

optimal_actions.action: Order MRI brain with dedicated epilepsy protocol (3T, thin-cut coronal T1/FLAIR/T2/DWI through hippocampi, gadolinium).
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MRI-negative — no hippocampal sclerosis, focal cortical dysplasia, or neoplasm; epilepsy-protocol MRI is essential to not miss subtle lesions, and a normal result in this context defines MRI-negative TLE.

optimal_actions.action: Order long-term video-EEG monitoring (eeg_type=video) to capture habitual ictal events, characterize electrographic onset, and lateralize the seizure focus.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Interictal right anterior temporal epileptiform discharges (F8/T4 phase reversal); ictal right anterior temporal electrographic onset confirming right temporal lobe localization; absence of independent left-sided discharges.

optimal_actions.action: Search medical literature for drug-resistant epilepsy definition, MRI-negative TLE surgical evaluation, and FDG-PET utility.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: ILAE 2010 drug-resistance definition (two appropriate AED failures); FDG-PET shows right temporal hypometabolism in 70-85% of TLE including MRI-negative cases; surgical outcomes in MRI-negative TLE are 50-60% seizure-free.

optimal_actions.action: Check drug interactions for current AED regimen (lamotrigine plus oral contraceptive pill) before any medication change.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: OCP (ethinyl estradiol) reduces lamotrigine levels by 40-60% via UGT induction — a clinically important pharmacokinetic interaction that must be accounted for; sulfonamide allergy precludes zonisamide.

optimal_actions.action: Order interictal FDG-PET (modality=FDG_PET) for metabolic localization when MRI is non-localizing.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Right temporal hypometabolism concordant with video-EEG right-sided ictal onset; PET asymmetry index <0.90 ipsilateral to the EEG focus supports surgical candidacy.

optimal_actions.action: Order comprehensive neuropsychological battery to lateralize memory function and assess surgical risk.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Non-verbal (visual) memory deficit with preserved verbal memory — material-specific profile consistent with right (non-dominant) temporal dysfunction; verbal memory preservation supports lower risk for post-operative language/verbal memory decline.

useless_tools.rationale: No clinical features of CNS infection, autoimmune encephalitis, or immunocompromise; lumbar puncture is not indicated in the routine evaluation of drug-resistant focal epilepsy.
No syncope-versus-seizure ambiguity and no cardiac symptoms; ECG does not contribute to the epilepsy localization workup in this presentation.
No convulsive syncope question, no cardiac embolic concern; echocardiogram is not indicated for this epilepsy workup.

Cardiac monitoring is reserved for syncope-versus-seizure differentiation; the semiology here (stereotyped focal awareness impairment with post-ictal confusion) is not consistent with cardiac syncope.
Head CT is inferior to MRI for epileptogenic substrate detection and adds ionizing radiation; MRI epilepsy protocol is the appropriate structural imaging modality.

sequence_constraints.reason: Structural cause (e.g., low-grade tumor) influences AED choice; MRI result should inform drug selection before interactions are checked.

critical_actions: Recognize that a normal MRI — including an epilepsy-protocol study — does not exclude epilepsy; 20-30% of drug-resistant TLE is MRI-negative, and these patients deserve full presurgical evaluation.
Do not accept a PNES diagnosis on the basis of normal MRI alone; stereotyped semiology, post-ictal state, nocturnal occurrence, and elevated prolactin all support an epileptic etiology.

Confirm drug resistance using ILAE 2010 criteria (failure of two appropriately chosen, tolerated AED trials at adequate doses and levels) before concluding that further AED escalation is the primary strategy.
Perform long-term video-EEG to capture habitual ictal events and confirm electrographic lateralization to the right temporal lobe.
Order interictal FDG-PET when MRI is non-localizing; right temporal hypometabolism concordant with EEG lateralization is sufficient to support surgical candidacy referral.
Refer the patient to a comprehensive epilepsy surgery center for multidisciplinary presurgical evaluation once multimodal concordance (EEG, PET, neuropsychology) is established.
contraindicated_actions: Do not diagnose PNES or discontinue epilepsy evaluation based solely on a normal MRI — normal structural imaging does not exclude focal epilepsy.
Do not continue cycling through additional AEDs indefinitely once the ILAE definition of drug resistance is met; surgical referral is the evidence-based next step.
Do not overlook the pharmacokinetic interaction between the oral contraceptive pill and lamotrigine when interpreting therapeutic drug levels or escalating doses.
Do not interpret right temporal PET hypometabolism as diagnostic of epilepsy in isolation; integrate with video-EEG and neuropsychological findings for localization.
key_reasoning_points: MRI-negative TLE is a real and well-characterized entity accounting for 20-30% of refractory temporal lobe epilepsy; a normal MRI must not terminate the epilepsy workup or prompt a PNES diagnosis.

The combination of right anterior temporal ictal EEG onset on video-EEG and right temporal hypometabolism on FDG-PET provides multimodal localization sufficient to support surgical candidacy even in the absence of a visible structural lesion.

Drug resistance is defined by the ILAE 2010 criteria as failure of two appropriate AED trials, not by duration of illness or number of dose escalations; once criteria are met, surgical evaluation is indicated.

The neuropsychological profile — selectively impaired non-verbal (visual) memory with intact verbal memory — is consistent with right (non-dominant) temporal lobe dysfunction and supports lateralization; this also informs the post-operative risk profile.

The OCP-lamotrigine pharmacokinetic interaction (UGT induction reducing lamotrigine levels by 40-60%) is clinically relevant and must be considered when assessing apparent drug resistance and when planning any medication change.
Tier per the July 2026 clinical review: Laboratory testing does not diagnose focal epilepsy; it addresses a provoked seizure or a metabolic mimic when one is suspected.

red_herrings.data_point: Normal epilepsy-protocol MRI at two institutions (initial 1.5T and current 3T), leading to a psychiatry diagnosis of psychogenic non-epileptic spells at the referring center.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor the diagnostic conclusion on structural imaging normality and label the episodes as PNES, thereby terminating the epilepsy workup prematurely.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: MRI-negative TLE is real; 20-30% of drug-resistant TLE has normal MRI. The correct path is multimodal localization with video-EEG and FDG-PET, not dismissal of an epileptic etiology.

red_herrings.data_point: Psychiatry consultation at referring center concluding 'most consistent with psychogenic non-epileptic spells superimposed on a migrainous diathesis.'
red_herrings.intended_effect: Accept the PNES label and redirect toward psychotherapy rather than presurgical epilepsy evaluation.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Ictal fear with stereotyped semiology, left-sided automatisms, post-ictal confusion, nocturnal occurrence, and elevated post-ictal prolactin are inconsistent with PNES; electrographic ictal correlate on video-EEG definitively excludes PNES.
